title: Securing your Azure Storage Account: a guide to enabling Business Central-only access using Network Security Perimeter.
summary: Securing Azure Storage accounts accessed by Business Central using Network Security Perimeter (NSP) creates a logical network boundary that restricts access by IP address rules, allowing organizations to protect cloud resources while maintaining Business Central integration without traditional networking overhead.
key_points: NSP provides modern security by creating logical boundaries at the resource level rather than subnet level, initially logging access in Transition mode before enforcing rules

Business Central accesses to Azure Storage must be authorized using IP addresses from the Dynamics365BusinessCentral service tag, which can be retrieved via PowerShell, Azure Management API, or downloadable JSON files
NSP can be created and managed through Azure Portal or Azure CLI, with steps including perimeter creation, profile definition, inbound rule configuration, and resource association
Organizations should validate legitimate Business Central traffic in Transition mode before switching to Enforced mode to block unauthorized access
NSP protects against unauthorized data access and exfiltration while simplifying compliance management compared to traditional Virtual Networks and Private Endpoints

quotes.text: NSP is a critical component of the underlying infrastructure of Business Central online (it restricts access to storage and SQL database).
quotes.why_it_matters: This shows NSP is already fundamental to how Business Central online protects resources, making it relevant for on-premises and cloud integrations

quotes.text: By establishing clear access boundaries and explicitly allowing only authorized traffic, you reduce security risks, simplify compliance, and maintain visibility into storage access patterns.
quotes.why_it_matters: This summarizes the practical business value: reduced risk, easier compliance, and transparency for access monitoring
